title: A variant-level cell test of 4-AP in STX1B epilepsy

sentences.text: This is a hypothesis, not a finding; its weakest link is the direction of effect, because STX1B variants can affect release in opposite directions.
Classify variants as release-down or release-up, then test whether 4-aminopyridine (4-AP) improves release in release-down neurons without worsening network excitability.
Use human iPSC-derived neurons, prioritizing the published STX1B G226R network-excitability assay and the SNAP25 I67N study as a template for 4-AP testing.
Ask the lab which variant models are available and which additional models would need to be built.
Measure release direction before treatment, then compare release and network excitability before and after 4-AP in the release-down class.
Confirm that the selected assays can distinguish release changes from network-excitability changes before proceeding.
Include untreated neurons from each tested variant and retain untreated release-up neurons as a classification comparator.

sections.heading: What result would change the plan

sentences.text: Stop expansion if release does not improve or network excitability worsens; a selective improvement would justify further variant-level cell testing, not patient treatment.
The graph contains no study testing this therapy class in STX1B-related epilepsies, and its STX1B pathway annotation is inferred rather than direct treatment evidence.
This release-down-only experiment would not establish what 4-AP does in release-up variants.
